plan.title: bug(pr): refuse Closes while the brief is still active, and exit wait-mergeable on P1

narratives.Description: Refuse --allow-close N while N has a running xbrief/active brief; waiter maps SHA-matched NEW_P0_P1 in-process. Bound lean 5705214194.
narratives.Overview:
## In plain English

A leftover-closeout PR during the v0.119.1 cut used `--allow-close` while the brief was still `active/running`. Greptile filed a P1. `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` then sat on that P1 for ~40 minutes instead of exiting. Stop that stall with two existing-gate compositions. Do not invent a new pipeline.

## Slice (this issue)

1. `task pr:check-closing-keywords --allow-close N` fails closed when issue N still has a brief in `xbrief/active/` with status `running`. Print: use `Refs` / `Tracking` until leftover-complete. Reuse `verify:orphan-active` / `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` — do not duplicate their predicate. `--allow-close` is intent-mode allowlist (#3015), not leftover-complete consent.

2. `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` treats a current-HEAD Greptile `NEW_P0_P1` as a terminal halt (exit 1, named outcome), same as `pr:watch` / `pr:finish-loop`. Do not poll to `--cap-minutes`. SHA-match still applies (a stale pre-push review is not NEW_P0_P1). Confidence 4/5 with a P1 is still P1.

Merge-time `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` is too late: Greptile has already filed.

## Incident

- v0.119.1 cut invented side PR #4622 for stale `docs/RULE-MAP.md` on master (issue #4621).
- `--allow-close 4621` passed intent mode while the brief was `active/running`.
- Greptile P1 + dogfood floor 5/5 observed 4/5.
- Waiter polled ~40 min. Operator killed it. Dropped Closes; leftover-complete after merge.

## Related (not this slice)

- #3015 `--allow-close` intent-mode allowlist
- #1056 `pr:watch` three-state (already exits NEW_P0_P1)
- #3875 other merge routes bypass closeout — sibling
- #2260 waiter proceeds on GitHub CLEAN+MERGEABLE; genuine P0/P1 still "block" by waiting, not by exiting

## Fallbacks if this slice does not arc as usable

If (1)+(2) is the wrong layer, too coupled, or a cheaper existing hook wins, pick one of these instead. Do not do all of them.

- **Release Phase 1 red-tip MUST.** `task release` Phase 1 fail-closed when default-branch CI is red (stale RULE-MAP). Prevents inventing the side PR. Larger: it is a release-pipeline gate, not the leftover-closeout stall.
- **`scope:activate` rebinds `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE`.** Release-cut occupancy still demanded a story pin for CHANGELOG. Wrong pin blocked writes and forced leftover ingest. Useful, but it is hook/session, not the P1 stall.
- **Step 5 named-cause prints vitest FAIL titles.** Production recut auto-hatched UNKNOWN because stdio swallowed FAIL names. Helps the next hatch, not this stall.

Do not start with: auto `docs:rule-map` on leftover-complete; lowering the Greptile floor to 4/5; extending `release-publish` mint to 8h.

## Acceptance

- `--allow-close N` + running brief in `xbrief/active/` for N → exit 1, names the brief path, suggests Refs.
- `--allow-close N` + no running brief for N (completed / no brief) → unchanged.
- `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` on a PR whose current-HEAD Greptile verdict is NEW_P0_P1 → exit 1 in one probe, no cap wait.
- SHA-mismatched stale P1 still waits / ignores as today.
- Tests for both predicates. No CHANGELOG policy loosen. No `minGreptileConfidence` change.

Refs #3015, #1056, #2260, #3875, #4621, #4622

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-16T16:59:42Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Pinned to dispatch SHA `3be4b339705132fe8c9d1f1b7a8c08425b255ee2`. Input ceiling `5701187198` (Stop 1 write-back). Open critique, N=1. Audit-targets: none.

The two named compositions can bind, but not as a subprocess swap or as a call to either named gate's `evaluate()`. Slice 1 needs a new fail condition over an existing enumerator. Slice 2 needs the finish-loop mapping into the waiter, not `pr:watch` exit codes fed through `classifyMonitorOutcome`.

## 1. Waiter "same as pr:watch" cannot bind through the existing monitor classifier

blocks-the-design

Evidence (re-run, not a line cite):

- `packages/core/src/pr-monitor/monitor.ts` at this SHA loops readiness until `merge_ready` or cap. There is no `NEW_P0_P1` return. Genuine P0/P1 is a HARD block in `verdictBlockIsSoftOnly` (`packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/mergeability.ts`), so GitHub CLEAN+MERGEABLE does not override it, and the monitor still waits out `--cap-minutes`. That is the ~40 minute stall.
- `packages/core/src/pr-watch/watch.ts` returns `NEW_P0_P1` / exit 1 on the first SHA-matched `hasBlocking` probe.
- `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/classify.ts` `classifyMonitorOutcome`: monitor exit 1 without `monitor_result: CAP-REACHED` or `ABSENT-REQUIRED` is `config-error` and `EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR` (2). Locked in `classify.test.ts` as `#2673`.
- `packages/core/src/finish-loop/pr-finish-loop.ts` already maps `watch().exitCode === EXIT_NEW_P0_P1` in-process to `ACTION_REQUIRED`. It does not pass `pr:watch` exit codes into `classifyMonitorOutcome`.
- Waiter three-state is 0 merged / 1 timeout-or-escalation / 2 config. Watch three-state is 0 CLEAN / 1 NEW_P0_P1 / 2 error. The integers are not the same vocabulary.

Failure mode: an implementer reads "same as `pr:watch` / `pr:finish-loop`" plus "do not invent a new pipeline" as replacing `runMonitor` with `pr:watch`. First current-HEAD P1 then becomes waiter outcome `config-error` and process exit 2. Address-path recovery (drop Closes, fix, re-run) is the config-retry path. The acceptance line "exit 1 in one probe, named outcome" fails. Reading "no new pipeline" as a ban on a named waiter outcome leaves no implementation that satisfies the acceptance line, because the existing classifier is the composition surface.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind until slice 2 names the finish-loop mapping as in-scope existing-gate composition: one SHA-matched `pr:watch` probe (or the same `hasBlocking` detector `#1056` already shares) before the cap loop, a new `classifyMonitorOutcome` discriminator with a named waiter outcome, exit 1, and `#2673` config-error kept for empty/non-CAP exit 1. That mapping is not a third pipeline. Subprocess-swap of `runMonitor` for `pr:watch` is out.

## 2. "Reuse their predicate" is not the running-brief fail condition the acceptance line names

sharpens-framing

Evidence:

- Acceptance: `--allow-close N` plus a brief in `xbrief/active/` with status `running` for N → exit 1.
- `verify:orphan-active` (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts`, `commands.md` at this SHA): fail when a running brief's origins are already closed or the linked PR is already merged. Post-close orphan. Pre-close `--allow-close` never hits it.
- `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` (`packages/core/src/pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts`): fail when the PR's structured closing refs name a running brief whose acceptance criteria are unattested. `if (gate.ok) continue` — an attested running brief passes. The gate also keys off forge closing references, not the CLI allowlist.
- Both modules keep a private `listActiveRunningBriefs`. It is not exported. The scan is already duplicated. Neither `evaluate()` is the acceptance fail condition.

Failure mode: compose by calling either `evaluate()`. Leftover-closeout with attested (or empty-gate) criteria still gets `--allow-close` while the brief is running — the incident shape. Orphan-active stays silent until after close. Acceptance tests for "running brief → exit 1" fail, or the tests are written against the wrong predicate and the stall returns.

Disposition consequence: bind the acceptance fail condition (running-for-N). Recut "do not duplicate their predicate" to: reuse the running-brief enumerator and `collectGithubRefs` matching (repo-qualified, same as closeout), do not call either gate's `evaluate()`, do not copy the orphan-signature or unattested-AC verdict. Extracting the already-duplicated enumerator is reuse, not a new pipeline.

## 3. Slice 2 must key `hasBlocking` / `NEW_P0_P1`, not HARD-block

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `verdictBlockIsSoftOnly` returns false for P0/P1, ERRORED, `shouldNotMerge`, and confidence below `minGreptileConfidence`. Dogfood floor 5 makes confidence 4/5 HARD even with zero findings. `pr:watch` `NEW_P0_P1` is SHA-matched `probe.hasBlocking` from the findings channel, not the confidence holdout. Watch order: CLEAN first, then `hasBlocking`. P1 plus 4/5 is `NEW_P0_P1`. 4/5 with no P1 is not CLEAN and not `NEW_P0_P1`; it polls toward stall/timeout.

Failure mode: early-exit on `verdictBlockIsSoftOnly === false` (or on any readiness failure string) turns a 4/5 dogfood wait into an immediate halt. That is an operational change to the floor while the acceptance line says no `minGreptileConfidence` change. The incident's "4/5 with a P1 is still P1" sentence is then implemented as "4/5 is a halt."

Disposition consequence: slice 2 cites `pr:watch` `hasBlocking` / `VERDICT_NEW_P0_P1`. Sub-floor confidence without P1 stays a wait. Stale-SHA P1 stays non-terminal (already `watch.ts` SHA-match). Do not classify from readiness failure English.

## 4. Slice 1 is the CLI `--allow-close` path; live `--pr` still skips intent

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts` — when `args.pr !== null && closeAllow.size === 0`, intent hits are dropped. `.github/workflows/branch-gate.yml` at this SHA runs `task pr:check-closing-keywords -- --pr "$PR_NUMBER" --mode both` and comments that live `--pr` does not fail `#3015` intent without `--allow-close`. CI cannot carry that allowlist.

Failure mode: an implementer "fixes" leftover Closes by making the branch-gate `--pr` run fail when a running brief exists. That recuts `#3015`'s live skip, which this slice said it would not. Conversely, treating slice 1 as sufficient closeout means a PR that already contains `Closes` without a local `--allow-close` still auto-closes on merge; only slice 2 (P1 halt) is the backstop for that path, and the halt does not strip the keyword.

Disposition consequence: keep slice 1 on the CLI allowlist (`--allow-close N` plus running-for-N, print Refs/Tracking, name the brief path). Record live `--pr` skip as unchanged `#3015`. Slice 2 is the merge-path backstop when Closes already landed. Other merge routes stay `#3875`.

## 5. Running-brief enumerator is private and already copied

footnote

`listActiveRunningBriefs` exists in both `orphan-active/evaluate.ts` and `pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts` and is not exported. Closeout takes a lifecycle root; orphan-active takes a project root and resolves the layout. Reuse means extract-and-call, not a third copy inside `pr-closing-keywords`. Pass `--project-root` the same way closeout reads the working tree (worktree leftover-closeout otherwise scans the wrong `xbrief/active/`).

## Injection / swarm lens

This slice changes issue-close authority (`--allow-close` / `Closes`), merge authority (`pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge`), untrusted review text (Greptile/SLizard bodies), and shared lifecycle state (`xbrief/active/` running briefs, including dest worktrees).

- Authority: `--allow-close` stays the `#3015` intent-mode allowlist. Running-for-N is an extra refuse on that allowlist, not leftover-complete consent and not one-PR-unit consent. Do not mint close authority from a body trailer or from a passing attestable check.
- Untrusted input: Greptile comment bodies are untrusted. Compose `pr:watch`'s canonical detector (`detect` / `resolveFindingsChannel` / SHA-match). Do not parse P1 from comment prose inside the waiter. A second detector is the `#1056` defect class.
- Shared state / worktrees: the running-brief read is the worker tree (`--project-root` / cwd), same basis closeout already documents for merge-time. Occupancy and dest-lock stay on `#4020` / `#4066`; this slice does not grow them.
- Concurrency: the waiter halt must not disable GitHub auto-merge as a side effect of a P1 address-path (head-gate already disables on stale approval). P1 halt is "do not merge, do not wait"; it is not revoke-approval unless HEAD moved.

## Road not taken

Rejected calling `verify:orphan-active` / `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` `evaluate()` from `--allow-close` (wrong fail condition; finding 2). Rejected replacing `runMonitor` with a `pr:watch` subprocess (exit-code collision; finding 1). Rejected early-exit on every HARD block (floor-change in effect; finding 3). Rejected making branch-gate live `--pr` fail intent for running briefs (`#3015` recut; finding 4). Rejected the issue-body fallbacks (release Phase 1 red-tip, `scope:activate` rebind, Step 5 FAIL titles): they do not stop this leftover-closeout stall.

Chosen: new running-for-N refuse on the existing allowlist, plus finish-loop-style `NEW_P0_P1` mapping in the waiter classifier.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected position: leftover-closeout is already `verify:pr-closeout-attestable`'s job, so `--allow-close` should call that `evaluate()` and the waiter should keep waiting on HARD blocks because `#2260` only authorized GitHub CLEAN override for soft verdicts. Flip: attestable is last-before-merge and keyed on unattested AC plus forge closing refs; the incident is pre-merge Greptile P1 plus a local allowlist that currently suppresses intent. Merge-time attestable never ran in the stall (monitor sits in front of it in `cascade.ts`). Waiting on HARD P1 is the measured defect. The position flips if the acceptance line is recut to unattested-AC-only and if P1 wait-to-cap is accepted.
